source.title: Multi-Turn Jailbreaks Steer Along Directions Single-Turn Safety Did Not Shape

page_placements.theme: Jailbreak mechanisms: suppressing the refusal direction, direction-guided attacks, and routes outside the single-turn direction

record.tranche_reason: The study tests interventions on reconstructed refusal and drift directions and argues that multi-turn jailbreak drift can bypass, rather than suppress, the refusal readout; it also reports limits on causal interpretation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many DCD detection and rescue results, but those do not by themselves measure suppression of the refusal direction or the causal role of that direction, so they are not recorded as rows here. The direct refusal-readout and direction-intervention results, plus the geometry and its controls, are included.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a detector paper, but three results bear on the claim. (1) Across multi-turn attack turns, the refusal-direction readout, measured against matched benign conversations, stays near zero (Fig. 1b; App. E). The authors call this bypass rather than suppression, which argues against V3 for content-drift multi-turn attacks. (2) Setting the Arditi refusal coordinate to its benign value at one layer raises harmful compliance on Llama-3.1-8B but not on Mistral-7B (bears on V1). (3) Activation additions along the reconstructed refusal direction do not separate from random directions (bears on V1 induction).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct but should lead with the main claims. Multi-turn jailbreaks move along history-dependent drift directions that the single-turn refusal–harmfulness plane does not span. The refusal readout is bypassed rather than eroded (limited to content-drift attacks). DCD is a detection readout, not a causal lever. The refusal-coordinate positive control works on Llama-3.1-8B and is inconclusive on Mistral-7B. Activation additions are inconclusive about direction-specific causality.
record.recipe_differences: The original refusal direction is reconstructed for comparison, but the main direction is learned from context differentials between attack and benign conversations. Causal tests edit one coordinate at one readout depth; the study does not perform the original all-layer, all-position refusal-direction ablation or weight editing.
record.method_sensitivity: The causal result differs by target: the refusal-coordinate edit changes compliance on Llama-3.1-8B but is indistinguishable from controls on Mistral-7B. The paper also reports that effects of large activation additions overlap across directions.

fits_no_version.finding: The jointly fitted multi-turn drift direction retains only 0.03–0.09 of its norm in the refusal–harmfulness plane, within the shuffled-label null on all five models. Held-out refusal/harmfulness directions retain 0.79–0.96. The result extends to the Qwen-3 0.6B–32.8B and Qwen-2.5-72B ladder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-turn jailbreak drift occupies directions largely outside the single-turn refusal–harmfulness plane.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing or patching the drift coordinate does not reduce harmful compliance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The multi-turn drift direction is a predictive readout but is not shown to cause harmful compliance.

record.code_released: not stated (the supplementary material is said to include the detector and analysis code)
record.problems: Causal tests edit a single coordinate at one depth rather than intervening across layers and positions. The interchange test uses 41 conversations selected for original jailbreak success; low replay compliance limits power to detect the predicted reduction on the drift edit. The refusal-coordinate result differs by target, and the larger activation-addition effects overlap with random controls. No general-capability preservation test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant refusal-direction outcome was omitted. DCD detector AUROC, rescue, and adaptive-attack results are not listed because they evaluate the detector rather than measuring refusal-direction suppression or causal mediation.

untested.parts: All-layer, all-position directional ablation; capability preservation; induction of refusal on harmless prompts by adding the direction at the original's scale.
Single-turn jailbreaks (suffix, template attacks); adversarial training against refusal-direction ablation.
Whether refusal itself is multi-dimensional, a cone, or affine. The 48-dim subspace analysis concerns the drift axis, not refusal.

missing.what: The refusal-score mechanism contrast across all ten Crescendo/Echo Chamber × target cells. Isolated refusal score reaches only 0.42–0.78 AUROC. Projecting the context differential onto the refusal direction does not separate attack from benign. This generalizes r17 beyond the unspecified Fig. 1b model.
missing.locator: Appendix E, 'The mechanism contrast holds across cells'; §4.2

missing.what: The isolated-turn refusal score rises as attacks proceed but never becomes separating (Fig. 1a). Attack and benign isolated-score medians are 0.1 vs −0.2.

record.verdict_notes: Main fixes: Table 1 positive-control values for Mistral and Qwen were misread (r6, r7). r11 is better described as partial. The Mistral failure (r12) is relabelled limits_scope rather than challenges, because a one-layer coordinate patch is not the all-layer ablation V1 specifies. Arditi et al. note that single-layer ablation can be reconstructed by later layers, and this paper notes the same. The activation-addition label now cites only V1-linked rows (r13, r14), not r15/r16. r19 state is changed to absent. The V3 challenge is scoped to content-drift multi-turn attacks, as the authors themselves restrict it and cite contrary multi-turn findings.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the difference-in-means refusal direction at every layer and position; does not establish that such ablation removes refusal while preserving general capabilities; harmless-request refusal induction is not established.
No training against direction ablation is evaluated; the attack evidence concerns the studied multi-turn attacks and does not establish a universal mechanism for jailbreaks.
Does not test whether refusal itself is affine, conic, or composed of a dominant direction plus other refusal directions.
Does not directly compare a harmfulness judgment with a refusal decision as separate outcomes.
Directions are fitted separately by model; no cross-language transfer or transfer of one direction across model variants or from base to instruct is tested.
No refusal-training intervention or comparison of training schedules.

relation.reason: It reconstructs the Arditi refusal direction and reports its own results on it: plane projection, Fig. 1b readout, interchange patch and activation addition.

tranche.reason: §4.3 'Bypass, not erosion' gives results and an explicit argument that content-drift multi-turn attacks do not suppress the refusal direction. That challenges V3 as worded. The paper also runs a refusal-coordinate positive control relevant to V1.

source_check.notes: Table 1 gives four values per model in the order refusal, harmfulness, w, null; r6 and r7 were misread, the other rows are right. The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1–l4 follow the order of the verdicts. Checkpoints (Table 5): Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, gemma-2-9b-it, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct. The refusal direction comes from AdvBench harmful vs matched harmless prompts. The ICLR footer addressed to human reviewers is not an instruction to an AI.

statements.correction: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. Refusal coordinate set to its benign value at the readout layer while the model answers the final payload. 41 replayed judge-confirmed jailbreaks, Granite Guardian judge in response mode. Compliance 0.293, change +0.049. Drift edit also +0.049; random edit +0.073. Authors: the Mistral result remains inconclusive. The same edit on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct raised compliance 0.098→0.317 (9 flips toward compliance, 0 back, p=0.004).
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the text does state the Mistral checkpoint (Table 5). 'Does not mediate' overstates the result: the authors call it inconclusive, and it comes from a single-coordinate, one-depth patch.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, larger-scale activation additions; prompt set, scale and baseline not stated. Refusal 0.417 for the refusal direction, 0.462 for w, 0.438–1.000 for three random directions. Authors: cannot tell a direction-specific effect from nonspecific perturbation. On Mistral-7B, large additions reduce coherence.
statements.problem: The text does not say which prompts the additions were applied to, so they are not stated to be harmless or benign. It gives no baseline refusal rate and calls the result inconclusive. The study therefore cannot be filed under 'weak or none' induction.
